editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Live-Aquatic Trade That Bali Bars for PMA
editorial.standfirst: Retailing ornamental fish, aquatic seed and other live, non-food aquatic life can be wholly foreign-owned nationally—but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium closes the PMA registration route.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47753 concerns the retail sale of live fish and other live aquatic organisms that are not intended for consumption. Its scope is precise about the stock: ornamental fish, pearl oysters, sponges, milkfish fry, shrimp fry, fish seed and clear lobster seed are all named examples. What binds them is their live, non-food character. The activity is defined less by a single species than by a particular kind of aquatic material, with seed forms sitting alongside more familiar ornamental and marine organisms.

Registration is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters. The record makes this one retail activity available from micro through large-scale operation, rather than limiting it to a narrow size band. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In direct terms, the national position permits a foreign investor to own the business fully. The listed national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali changes the practical result decisively. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today: its Bali status is blocked by risk class. The supplied reason is specific. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is recorded as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope. Bali’s stated moratorium prohibits PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, permanently. It took effect on May 13, 2026, according to the cited gubernatorial letter. This is a registration block, not a different national foreign-ownership ceiling.

The two positions must therefore be read without blurring them. The national record offers an open PMA status and a 100% ceiling; Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium nevertheless closes PMA registration for the activity. Neither fact cancels the other. For a founder assessing this retail trade in live, non-food aquatic life, the crucial distinction is geographic: national foreign ownership may be fully open, while the Bali registration route is unavailable. It is the distinction that prevents national openness from being mistaken for permission to register PMA in Bali.
